justification: New Section 'Structures & Records' in the conveyancing PDF (Stage 1 of 2) — the product's highest-liability text. It lists the subject lot's DA/CDC application records and, where structure detection runs (Stage 2), raises a structure with no matching record as a FACTUAL QUESTION, never an allegation. The defining constraint: no rendered string on any branch may state or imply a structure is unapproved/illegal/unauthorised/non-compliant/a breach/without consent. Wrong output here is a defamation or negligent-misstatement claim, so the no-verdict-word guard, three-state failure handling, fail-closed council resolution and adversarial wording review are the core of this change.

pre_impl.existing_data: Stage 1 uses ONLY application records, no imagery/detection call. Reuses pre_da_history.get_da_events + get_pcc_events (live OnlineDA/OnlineCDC, records begin ~2019) + _extract_da_fields shape + the _LGA_TO_COUNCIL ePlanning name map. Verified live 2026-07-07: 14 Stanley St Concord resolves 10+ DA/CDC records once the council is mapped to 'City of Canada Bay Council'. Bowral (Wingecarribee) is unmapped and fails closed to 'Not assessed'. The conveyancing pipeline holds NO structure detection today, so Stage 1 renders records + the honest 'detection not run' state; the gap machinery is built and tested but dormant until Stage 2.
pre_impl.assumption_mismatch: A live code check caught a silent-wrong-result: the pipeline derives the LEP council name ('Canada Bay Council') but OnlineDA requires the exact 'City of Canada Bay Council' — an unmapped name returns zero rows, which would have printed a FALSE 'no applications on record'. Fixed by _resolve_eplanning_council + fail-closed: an unresolved council renders 'Not assessed', never a false negative. An adversarial legal red-team also found the original gap sentence built the 'unapproved' imputation by ordering (visible structure -> no record -> interrogate vendor); the sentence was restructured to lead with the data-window limitation and carry an explicit non-imputation line.
pre_impl.new_vs_existing: Reused: pre_da_history fetchers + council map; the get_*_live wrapper pattern; the parallel-future executor of PR #674/#689/#691; the PDF section pattern of the shipped sibling sections. New: a floor-simple reconciliation builder, a fail-closed ePlanning-council resolver, and the no-verdict-word wording. NO new detection or fetcher code; NO imagery call in Stage 1; the brief and exempt_screening (deliberately unwired, #490) are untouched.
pre_impl.external_source_error: Records lookup failed or council unresolved -> (None, 'failed') -> the section states 'Not assessed', never an implied absence of applications. Records ran and found none -> the hedged 'no applications appear ... this is common for established properties ... not, on its own, a finding' sentence. Address matching is fuzzy text (the Portal keys nothing to a lot id), so the heading is 'Applications matched to this address' with a caveat that nearby same-street records may appear — no overclaim of exclusivity.
pre_impl.frontend_type: No frontend or API-contract change: the section is a PDF-render addition behind two generate_pdf keyword args (structures_records, structures_records_status) defaulting to None. The free-tier JSON, the pipeline cache and the Next.js components are untouched; jest and tsc see no new types.
pre_impl.user_failure_mode: The catastrophic failure is a reader inferring a structure is unauthorised (defamation of the vendor) or reading a professional guarantee into the section (negligent misstatement / ACL s18). Pinned by: an exhaustive test that renders EVERY branch and fails if any verdict framing appears; the gap sentence restructured after an adversarial red-team to lead with the limitation + a non-imputation line; the fail-closed council resolver that prevents a false 'no records'; the confidence floor that drops low-confidence detections; and the gap string kept DORMANT in Stage 1 (no detections) so the highest-risk text reaches no reader until Stage 2, which is gated on review + legal sign-off.

functions.name: build_structures_records_lines
functions.input: the subject-lot DA/CDC records list (or None / [] ), an optional detections list (None in Stage 1), and a records_status flag
functions.output: a render plan of only verdict-free strings: intro, verbatim record lines, a hedged no-records or Not-assessed status line, any hedged gap lines, and the detection-not-run note
functions.if_none: records None or status failed returns not_assessed with a 'Not assessed' status line; [] returns the hedged 'no applications appear' sentence — the two are kept distinct so a failed lookup never reads as a checked absence

functions.name: get_structures_records_live
functions.input: the pipeline-derived council name and the property address
functions.output: a tuple of the DA+CDC records list and an 'ok' status when the council resolves to an ePlanning-accepted name, else (None, 'failed')
functions.if_none: an unresolved council or a fetch exception returns (None, 'failed') so the section states 'Not assessed' — failing closed is deliberate because an unmapped council silently returns zero rows and would otherwise print a false 'no applications on record'

functions.name: _resolve_eplanning_council
functions.input: a derived council name in any of the LEP / DB / plain forms
functions.output: the exact OnlineDA/OnlineCDC-accepted council string via the shared _LGA_TO_COUNCIL map plus a local confirmed-live supplement, matching directly, by key, or after stripping LGA suffixes
functions.if_none: returns None when the name cannot be resolved to an accepted ePlanning string, so the caller fails closed rather than issuing a lookup that returns a misleading zero

values.value: app_type / dev_type / date / status / pan rendered verbatim into each application-record line
values.nullable: yes — any record field can be absent from the ePlanning response
values.guard_at: scripts/generate_conveyancing_report.py:2788 (each field falls back to a stated 'not stated in the record'; the raw status token, e.g. Determined/Refused, is rendered as-is and never rewritten to 'approved')
values.if_missing: the line states the field is not stated in the record; no value is invented and the record status is never upgraded to an approval word

values.value: detection confidence gating whether a structure may generate a gap line
values.nullable: yes — a detection may carry no confidence
values.guard_at: scripts/generate_conveyancing_report.py:2812 (_STRUCT_CONFIDENCE_FLOOR: a detection below the floor is dropped and never produces a gap line; None confidence is treated as usable only in tests)
values.if_missing: a low-confidence detection (a shadow or vegetation mis-segmentation) is dropped, so it cannot manufacture a reconciliation gap

values.value: the resolved ePlanning council name feeding the OnlineDA CouncilName filter
values.nullable: yes — an unmapped council resolves to None
values.guard_at: scripts/generate_conveyancing_report.py:2308 (_resolve_eplanning_council returns None for anything not in the accepted set/map)
values.if_missing: a None resolution fails the whole lookup closed to 'Not assessed' — the exact-match filter would otherwise return zero and read as a false absence

queries: N/A — no SQL changed; the records come from the live NSW ePlanning OnlineDA/OnlineCDC endpoints via the reused pre_da_history fetchers

break_it.scenario: A structure approved in 2005 (pre-Portal) shows as a reconciliation gap
break_it.what_happens: Without the data-window hedge the reader infers the structure is unauthorised; a 2005 approval simply predates the ~2019 Portal records
break_it.how: the gap sentence leads with 'records available to us begin around 2019 and do not include ...' and names 'one predating the record window' as an expected cause, plus a 'not, on its own, a finding about the structure' non-imputation line

break_it.scenario: An exempt-development shed (no application required) shows as a gap
break_it.what_happens: A reader infers the shed is unauthorised when it lawfully needs no application at all
break_it.how: the sentence names 'a structure that is exempt development and needs no application' as the FIRST expected cause; the feature never attempts exemption determination (exempt_screening stays unwired)

break_it.scenario: The pipeline derives a council name OnlineDA does not accept (e.g. Canada Bay, Wingecarribee)
break_it.what_happens: The exact-match CouncilName filter returns zero rows and the section prints a FALSE 'no applications on record' for a property that has many
break_it.how: _resolve_eplanning_council maps the name to the accepted ePlanning string or returns None; an unresolved council fails the lookup closed to 'Not assessed' — verified live: Concord now resolves records, Bowral (Wingecarribee unmapped) renders 'Not assessed'

break_it.scenario: A SAM false positive (shadow or vegetation) is detected as a structure
break_it.what_happens: A non-existent structure generates a gap line and an implied irregularity
break_it.how: detections below _STRUCT_CONFIDENCE_FLOOR are dropped before any gap line is built; the section never asserts a structure exists as fact (Stage 2 wording is 'visible in imagery' with a date)

break_it.scenario: The application-records lookup errors part-way through report generation
break_it.what_happens: An empty section reads as 'no applications', a false checked-clean on a failed lookup
break_it.how: a failed fetch returns (None, 'failed') and the section states 'Not assessed — the application-records lookup was unavailable', distinct from the successful-empty sentence

break_it.scenario: A future edit introduces a verdict word (unapproved/illegal/unauthorised/...) on any code path
break_it.what_happens: The report defames the vendor by stating or implying a structure is unlawful
break_it.how: an exhaustive test renders every builder branch and fails if any forbidden framing appears; a second central runtime guard in test_conveyancing_truth.py repeats the scan; the gap string is dormant in Stage 1 regardless

break_it.scenario: The fuzzy address match lists a neighbouring same-street property's application as this property's
break_it.what_happens: A record for 16 Stanley St is presented as the history of 14 Stanley St — a factual overclaim on a legal document
break_it.how: the heading is 'Applications matched to this address' (not 'on record for this property') and a caveat states matching is by address text and may include nearby same-street properties — check the PAN before relying on it

post_merge.db_reset: No — no database schema or data changes anywhere in this branch
post_merge.secrets: No — the ePlanning OnlineDA/OnlineCDC endpoints are public NSW services requiring no keys
post_merge.other_repo: No — self-contained in scripts and services plus their tests
post_merge.manual_verify: Yes — this is the product's highest-liability text: a human (ideally a lawyer) must read every Section 12/13 sentence against the no-verdict rule before Stage 2 is built, since Stage 2 makes the dormant gap sentence user-visible. Also regenerate the Concord + Bowral PDFs through the deployed Railway pipeline (Concord resolves records, Bowral fails closed to 'Not assessed').
